svg.aria-label: Animated diagram of a Cnt cluster where the replica count follows each repository's traffic. An S3 object store band sits above a row of cluster nodes; below them, a band marked with a globe stands for git clients across the web, sending heavy streams of pushes and pulls — many packets ride every lane at once. Every repository is an unlabeled tinted square whose side length follows the repository's size: a large monorepo is replicated on every node, three medium repositories keep a few replicas each, and well over a hundred tiny repositories keep a single replica on one node. The store itself holds no repository shapes at all, only a field of identical opaque objects: the WAL entries. Traffic travels as smaller solid squares in the repository's hue. Every push arrives at its repository's primary replica, marked with a dot, and appends one more object to the store; pulls are served by any replica. At any moment more than half of the tiny replicas are garbage-collected off their node's disk — shown as dashed empty squares — living only in the WAL. Replicas are constantly collected and rematerialized: a WAL read from S3 brings a slot back the moment a pull needs it, and idle slots fade back out.
